notes: Arduino Yún is not in the catalogue, so it is a new part type with Uno-style headers.
The breadboard is a small one drawn rotated: its 5-hole strips run horizontally. They are mapped to catalogue names as columns 1t, 4t and 5t, which are the picture rows 1, 4 and 5.

In the photo the black GND wire appears to end on the same strip as the resistor's lower leg and the LED's upper leg. That would short the resistor, so I followed the schematic. The wire goes on the LED cathode strip (5t) and the LED anode shares a strip with resistor leg 2 (4t).
The red wire goes to the header socket just left of pin 8, which is D9. The GND wire goes to the bottom-header GND next to VIN, taken as GND.1.
The LED's longer leg is the anode and connects to the resistor side. The cathode goes to GND.
The Yún and its Wi-Fi network, USB power and the software side are not part of the wiring graph.
